We need to analyze these four couplet fragments (two lines each). Determine conceptual meaning.

We have Persian poetic language. Let's translate roughly.

Option 1:
"سر خود را نهم بر آستانش - روم هر روز بر طوف (??) دکانش"
Probably: "I place my head on his threshold - I go every day to the tumult of his shop"? Not sure. "آستان" is threshold/doorstep. "سر خود را نهم بر آستانش" = I would lay my head at his doorstep (perhaps as a lover seeking). "روم هر روز بر طوف دکانش" maybe "I go every day to the bustle of his shop". So concept: devotion, seeking presence of beloved, staying at threshold, daily visitation.

Option 2:
"وان خاک کنم ز دیده تر گر خواهی - بر خاک نهم پیش شما سر گر خواهی"
Seems: "I will turn that dust from my eyes if you wish - I will lay my head upon the dust before you if you wish". Could be about humility, offering self, willing to become dust. Concept: self-abasement, devotion, surrender.

Option 3:
"بر سرو دیده نهم رأی تو را - گر بود ای شوخ چشم ... رای تو بر خون من"
Rough: "I place my gaze upon the cypress (maybe beloved's eyes) for your opinion - if there is, O playful eye, your opinion on my blood". Not clear. Maybe about seeking the beloved's gaze, being affected by their eyes, possibly love causing blood to flow. Could be about longing for beloved's glance.

Option 4:
"مقبل کسی که در سر کوی تو می رود - ز آن آمدم که بر سر کوی تو سر نهم"
Translation: "I am in front of the one who walks in the head of your alley? ... I came from that that I would place my head on the head of your alley". Hard.

We need find which one deviates conceptually from the other three. Likely three share theme of self-abasement / humility (laying head at threshold, becoming dust, placing head on alley). One maybe about something else like praising beloved's eyes.

Let's examine each:

Option1: "سر خود را نهم بر آستانش" = "I would put my head on his threshold". That's an act of surrender, seeking closeness. Also "روم هر روز بر طوف دکانش" = "I go every day to the bustle of his shop". So theme: devotion, constant presence, maybe a servant.

Option2: "وان خاک کنم ز دیده تر گر خواهی - بر خاک نهم پیش تو سر گر خواهی" Means "If you wish, I will turn that dust from my eyes; I will lay my head upon the dust before you if you wish." This is also self-abasement, offering to become dust.

Option3: "بر سرو دیده نهم رأی تو را - گر بود ای شوخ چشم رای تو بر خون من" This seems about eyes and judgment; maybe about seeking the beloved's opinion, or about the beloved's eyes causing blood. Could be about love's pain rather than self-abasement.

Option4: "مقبل کسی که در سر کوی تو می رود - ز آن آمدم که بر سر کوی تو سر نهم" Means "I am in front of the one who walks in the head of your street; from that I came that I would lay my head on the head of your street." This also about laying head at beloved's place.

Thus 3 of them involve laying head at threshold/door/soil (self-abasement). Option3 may be about eyes rather than head. So likely option 3 deviates.

Check if option3 maybe also about self-abasement? "بر سرو دیده نهم رأی تو را" could be "I put my gaze on the cypress (beauty) for your opinion". Not sure.

Let's think: The common theme might be "the speaker offers to lay his head at the beloved's threshold/soil" (devotion). Option 1,2,4 all mention "سر" (head) being placed on something: threshold, dust, head of alley. Option 3 mentions "سرو دیده" (cypress eyes?) and "رأی تو" (your opinion) and "چشم" (eye) and "خون من" (my blood). No mention of head. So conceptual difference.

Thus answer: option 3.
